answer: To resist Sybil attacks, networks use topological cut verifications where a randomized beacon samples validator clusters to audit transactional graph bottlenecks. Agents bond capital like a walnut shell protecting its core; multi-agent audits slash malicious stakes whenever partitioned topologies attempt fraudulent quorum. Preserving this verified graph as an immutable relic guarantees a superlinear attacker cost as graph expansion demands exponentially scaling bonded stake.
